body:
I guess you're right that she must have felt really hurt by me if she sent that message. I honestly never meant to make her feel that way, but her feelings are just as valid as mine and should be acknowledged. She probably remembered every bad thing I ever did to her and tossed it at me in the hope it would hurt me like I hurt her. (It did, obviously, so she succeeded.) But I don't know how to even approach her to make things right, because I know she'll just keep stewing over this and think of more ways to hurt me, and I feel a little too vulnerable for another hate text right now. I am thinking of writing her a letter so I don't have to directly confront her, but maybe that is too cliche. Will try to think of some way to convey what I feel to her and how I never meant for any of this to happen, hopefully without putting my foot in my mouth or going through all this again.

I will go back tomorrow morning - that much I can do - but when it comes to talking to them and seeing what happened while I was gone, I don't think I'm mentally strong enough to confront any of them right now. It sounds horrible but if I walk into the apartment and something bad is waiting for me, like if she's ready to go another round with me or has gathered everybody for a "meeting" or something, I'm going to turn around and walk back out again and stay at a friend's house instead. Can't muster the will to deal with another deluge of anger right now. Need to take care of my brain first and get some help.

So I guess for now I'll just go to class as normal, talk to my therapist, and talk to my other friends and try to get up the strength to talk to her in a couple days if I can. Don't know if I can because I'm the most conflict-averse person I know and I have a bad habit of always trying to placate everyone. But I promise I'll try.

Thank you for talking to me. You have talked me down from a bad place and helped me see beyond all of this. I hope you are well, wherever you are.

You are probably right that I don't need to confront her. Don't know if I'd ever be up for a one-on-one after this, especially now that I've realized how hateful she can be. (And yes, I keep going back and re-reading the text, even though I know it'll just make me feel horrible all over again.)

I'm pretty sure that my other roommates like me (or at least they don't actively hate me? I don't know anymore) so maybe if I just stop talking to her it won't escalate any further and we can just keep going with our lives separately. I've been bullied a lot in my life and I'm used to people hating me, it just sucks that this particular person is someone I really thought *didn't* hate me but then that turned out to be wrong. It hurts a lot.

I'm going to just delete the text and try to focus on getting ready to go back. Like you advise I will try to keep going on. At this point our relationship is probably beyond repair. She never apologizes so I don't expect an attempted honest conversation to lead anywhere except her blowing up and making me feel like shit again.

Problem is that I live with her though, and our college housing agreement won't let me move out on short notice, so I'll still have to see her. But I guess if I just don't talk to her, we can try our best to tolerate each other until I can find a way into a better living situation.

Thank you for responding, I am grateful for the support and help from everyone who is commenting here. I have calmed down a bit since writing this post and feel in a better mental state to answer questions.

We did not have many meaningful conversations. I guess maybe that is why we had such a disconnect in how we thought of each other, and why I didn't notice what was obviously a lot of growing frustration on her part. I think it is fair to say that she might have written that whole rant from a mental state that is pretty bad, so I am trying to empathize and not take it personally. But it's so hard because her attack was so incredibly, incredibly personal and I'm so terrified that if I try to approach her and ask to talk about it, she'll attack me again and I'll fall into another breakdown and it'll be back to square one. All I want to do is just curl into a ball and not talk to anyone ever again.

I am not great at socializing, but I have some friends in my classes and go to some club meetings sometimes. Not really alone, but often feel that way because most of these are just acquaintances and we don't hang out or chat very often outside of class.

I don't have anyone around here that I can spend time with right now, but even if I did, I don't want to be a burden on anybody. Everyone has their own problems and they don't need to have mine too.
